correctness.rationale: Positive determinant-one split matrices have a unique simultaneous Euclidean parent until a classified boundary matrix. The two inverse column additions increase both row lengths by one, giving exactly 2^u matrices of ordered row lengths (u,v), and torus-parameter symmetry converts this bijectively to knot types with component sizes {u,v}.

originality.rationale: Lin--Spreer report finite cutoff counts and their companion notebook computes them recursively, while classical work covers the free binary monoid of nonnegative unimodular matrices. Targeted searches found no prior all-size torus-knot census or the refined 2^u component-size theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem replaces a finite census computation by a closed formula for every canonical size, refines it by the two component sizes, explains the reported value 3049 at cutoff 19, and yields an exponential lower bound for actual triangulation-complexity counts.
